sections.title: Commercial Performance
sections.description: How revenue and margin developed, and where the work is coming from.

children.markdown:
How revenue and margin developed, and where the work is coming from.

**In this chapter:** At a Glance  ·  Revenue & Margin  ·  Growth

Revenue peaks in October while margin slides from ~43% to ~39%.

One project explains it: Santa Clara Ph2 overruns after the Sep 14 scope change.

**Next:** price scope changes before the hours are worked.
Which divisions and project types bring in revenue, and which earn the margin.

East runs structurally lower margin (NYC labor cost).

Industrial lags at ~23%: Newark Logistics Hub is discounted unit-price work.

**Next:** review unit-price discounts on East work.
Where the work is coming from.

Data center work keeps growing; Reno AI Campus mobilized Oct 1.

**Next:** staff Electrical BIM ahead of the data center ramp-up.

children.markdown:
Budget, schedule and margin risk across the project portfolio.

**In this chapter:** Portfolio Health  ·  Where Projects Drift
How many projects are running, and how many are at risk.

Santa Clara Ph2 is ~1,060 hours over plan; every other project is within ±4%.

**Next:** recover Santa Clara Ph2 through a change order.
How hours over plan turn into lost margin.
**Margin vs. Hours over Plan by Project**
**Gross Margin % by Week and Contract Type**

Fixed Fee margin drops from ~41% to ~29% after Sep 14: overrun on a capped fee.

Newark is on plan but earns the lowest margin: a price issue, not delivery.

**Next:** add a scope-change clause to Fixed Fee contracts.

children.markdown:
Clash coordination, rework and on-time delivery.

**In this chapter:** Clash Coordination  ·  Rework & Delivery
BIM clashes found, resolved and still open.

The detected-vs-resolved gap closes after the VEC Coordination Hub went live on Sep 1.

**Next:** roll the Hub out to all remaining projects.
What rework costs, and which service lines deliver on time.

Santa Clara Ph2 burns ~$61K in rework, about twice any other project.

Onsite QC was hit by the August laser-scanner calibration issue.

**Next:** add calibration checks to Onsite QC.

children.markdown:
Who we work for, and how each division compares.

Who we work for, and what we earn from them.

Westbrook Builders is the largest client; strategic clients bring ~60% of revenue.

Granite Underground earns the lowest margin (~30%) on discounted Civil Underground work.
How each division compares, and where the work is.

East bills the same rates but earns ~10 pts less margin.

Data center work sits entirely in West and Central; Nevada is Reno AI Campus.
What the four chapters add up to.
Santa Clara Ph2 explains most of the margin slide; price changes before the hours are worked.
Same rates, ~10 pts less margin: review unit-price discounts and NYC staffing.
